quiz.question: On July 21, 2026, the Department of Posts (Maharashtra Circle) released a customized 'My Stamp' to commemorate which of the following historical milestones?
options: 750th Birth Anniversary of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj
400th Birth Anniversary of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
700th Death Anniversary of Sant Namdev Maharaj
quiz.explanation: On July 21, 2026, the Maharashtra Circle of the Department of Posts released a customized 'My Stamp' to mark the 750th Birth Anniversary of Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj in Mumbai. The stamp was unveiled by Chief Postmaster General Ramchandra Kisan Jayabhaye and presented to Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar. Sant Dnyaneshwar was a 13th-century philosopher and saint of the Varkari tradition who authored the Dnyaneshwari.

quiz.question: In July 2026, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) granted official marketing authorization for India's first approved dengue vaccine. What is the brand name of this vaccine?
quiz.explanation: The CDSCO has officially approved Qdenga®, India's first-ever vaccine against dengue, manufactured by Germany-based Takeda GmbH. The vaccine is a live, attenuated tetravalent dengue vaccine engineered using recombinant DNA technology. It is approved for use in individuals aged 4 to 60 years and is administered in a two-dose regimen.

quiz.question: The Maharashtra Government in July 2026 launched the implementation of the 'Urban Challenge Fund' (UCF) across all 423 urban local bodies. What is the total outlay of the projects proposed under this fund?
quiz.explanation: The Maharashtra Urban Development Department issued a government resolution to implement the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF) to carry out development projects worth ₹44,800 crore. The campaign will run from 2025-26 to 2030-31 and aims to make cities financially self-reliant. It adopts a blended finance model where the central government covers up to 25% of costs, bank loans/municipal bonds/PPP cover at least 50%, and the state/municipal body covers the rest.

quiz.question: Under the Biological Diversity Act, the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) released ₹6.67 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism for 11 cotton-growing states in July 2026. Which state received the highest allocation under this disbursement?
quiz.explanation: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) released ₹6.67 crore under the ABS mechanism realized from Bayer Science & Innovation Pvt. Ltd. for cotton research. Among the eleven cotton-growing states, Maharashtra received the highest allocation of ₹2.41 crore, followed by Gujarat (₹1.38 crore) and Telangana (₹1.06 crore). The funds will support local State Biodiversity Boards in conserving biodiversity and promoting sustainable utilization.

quiz.question: In July 2026, NSE Indices Limited launched the Nifty500 Ahimsa Index. Which of the following sectors is explicitly excluded from this ethical investing index?
quiz.explanation: The Nifty500 Ahimsa Index, developed in partnership with the Ahimsa Foundation, tracks companies that operate free from animal cruelty. It explicitly excludes sectors involved in meat, dairy, poultry, leather, cosmetics, fashion using wool, and pharmaceutical companies engaging in animal testing. Additionally, commercial banks are excluded due to their financing of these non-compliant sectors.

quiz.question: Under the EPFO 3.0 reform phase announced in July 2026, which of the following frameworks is introduced to allow members to set a personalized retirement goal based on their desired pension?
quiz.explanation: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) announced the EPFO 3.0 reforms, which transition the organization toward a universal social security platform. A key feature is the Target Retirement Sum (TRS) framework, where members can define a personalized retirement goal and monitor accumulation progress on interactive digital dashboards. Retiring members can convert these sums into annuities or Systematic Withdrawal Plans (SWP).

quiz.question: The Karlapat bauxite block, which became a major prize of competition for India's leading industrial giants in July 2026, is located in which district of Odisha?
quiz.explanation: The Karlapat-Pollingpadar bauxite block is located in the Kalahandi district of Odisha and holds an estimated 207 to 220 million tonnes of greenfield bauxite deposits. This high-grade gibbsitic deposit lies adjacent to the ecologically sensitive Karlapat Wildlife Sanctuary and elephant corridor. Weathering of Precambrian khondalites and charnockites in the Eastern Ghats led to its formation.

quiz.question: What is the primary objective of the Central Government's 'Parivartan' scheme, which was approved for implementation in Delhi in July 2026?
options: Restoration of dried-up urban water bodies
Transitioning agricultural pump sets to solar energy
Replacing old, polluting commercial vehicles with BS-VI and electric vehicles
Rejuvenating urban public parks into biodiversity hotspots
quiz.explanation: The Delhi Cabinet approved the implementation of the Centre's 'Parivartan' scheme to reduce transport air pollution. The scheme incentivizes commercial operators to scrap aging, polluting commercial vehicles (such as trucks and buses) and replace them with BS-VI-compliant or electric vehicles. It offers relief from registration fees, interest subsidies, and motor vehicle tax exemptions.

quiz.question: In the newly released Index of Core Industries (ICI) series with the revised base year of 2022–23, which core sector has been assigned the largest weightage?
quiz.explanation: In the updated Index of Core Industries (ICI) series released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (with base year 2022–23), Electricity gained substantial weightage to become the largest sector at 30.932% (up from 19.85% in the 2011–12 series). Refinery Products, which previously held the largest weight, decreased to 22.572%. The updated index also expanded from eight to nine sectors with the inclusion of Iron Ore.

quiz.question: In Electrodynamic Suspension (EDS) systems used in ultra-high-speed Maglev trains (such as Japan's SCMAGLEV), which technology facilitates the suspension of the train body above the guideway?
options: Attractive force between C-shaped vehicle arms and the underside of steel tracks
Superconducting magnets cooled to cryogenic temperatures generating repulsive force
Compressed air cushions ejected at high velocities from side guides
Rotary induction motors interacting with permanent track magnets
quiz.explanation: Electrodynamic Suspension (EDS) relies on superconducting magnets cooled to cryogenic temperatures on the train body. As the train moves, these magnets induce currents in guideway coils, creating a repulsive magnetic force that hovers the train approximately 100 mm above the track. In contrast, Electromagnetic Suspension (EMS) uses attractive forces to levitate the train about 10 mm above steel tracks.
